title: Meta Connect 2025 Developer Keynote
summary: A single speaker-section assignment for Meta's 2025 developer keynote that grew into leading the design flow for the full presentation.
overview: Meta Connect's developer keynote brings together multiple speakers, products, and technical ideas inside one live presentation. I joined to develop concepts for a single speaker section, and the engagement grew into leading the design flow across the full keynote.

projectBrief.context: Meta Connect required a developer keynote that could connect multiple speakers, products, demonstrations, and technical ideas within one coherent experience.
projectBrief.challenge: Each section needed its own purpose and pacing while still feeling like part of the same keynote. The presentation system also had to support speaker introductions, transitions, technical explanations, product moments, and motion.
projectBrief.contribution: I began with concept work for one speaker section. The engagement expanded to leading the design flow for the full developer keynote, including concept development, narrative structure, storyboarding, slide layouts, motion direction, and production alignment.
projectBrief.approach: Establish visual and structural patterns that could carry across speakers and subjects while adapting to different content needs, using hierarchy, pacing, transitions, and repeatable layouts to help the audience follow the story.
projectBrief.outcome: The assignment grew from a single speaker section into leading the design flow for the full developer keynote.

blocks.title: From one section to the full keynote
blocks.body: I joined Meta Connect's 2025 developer keynote to develop concepts for a single speaker section. As the keynote took shape, the assignment grew into leading the design flow for the full developer keynote: concept development, narrative structure, storyboarding, slide layouts, motion direction, and alignment across the teams producing it.

images.alt: Meta Connect 2025 opening keynote stage, with a speaker introducing the event

blocks.title: Building a flexible keynote system
blocks.body: Each part of the keynote needed its own purpose and pacing while still reading as one continuous story. I worked on a set of repeatable title, section, and transition layouts that could carry across different speakers and subjects without losing a consistent visual language.

blocks.title: Supporting speakers and technical stories
blocks.body: The keynote moved between speaker introductions, technical walkthroughs, and product moments, each with its own pacing and information needs. The slides below are examples from the keynote, pulled from public event documentation since the original working files weren't retained; not every one pictured was designed by me, but together they show the kind of layouts and hierarchy the role was responsible for shaping.

blocks.title: The live experience
blocks.body: The keynote was delivered live, in front of an audience, across a multi-day event. The same layouts and pacing had to work on stage, not only on a slide.
